there is insufficient evidence to support the routine use of newborn screening for CF in the United States.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is important that we do not lose sight of the clinical utility of genetic tests, and the same applies to newborn screening.
the cost is not the problem.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the benefits and harms of genetic testing for newborns and children should be considered in the context of the health care system in which the test will be offered and interpreted, as well as in the context of a child's individual health care.
the benefits of genetic testing for cancer risk are not as clear as many people think.
we should be cautious in our enthusiasm for the clinical usefulness of genetic tests.
